Donyell Marshall was not confused with former basketball player Donny Marshall.
Donyell Lamar Marshall was born on May 18, 1973, in Reading, Pennsylvania.
Donyell Lamar Marshall graduated from Reading High School.
Donyell Lamar Marshall attended the University of Connecticut and played for their basketball program.
Donyell Lamar Marshall was a unanimous pick as Big East Player of the Year in 1993–94.
Donyell Lamar Marshall left college early to participate in the 1994 NBA draft.
Donyell Lamar Marshall was selected by the Minnesota Timberwolves after his junior year at the University of Connecticut, as the fourth overall pick in the 1994 NBA draft.
Donyell Lamar Marshall was traded from the Minnesota Timberwolves to the Golden State Warriors on February 18, 1995.
Donyell Lamar Marshall played with the Golden State Warriors until 2000.
Donyell Lamar Marshall was traded from the Golden State Warriors to the Utah Jazz in a four-team deal in 2000.
Donyell Lamar Marshall played alongside future Hall of Fame nominees Karl Malone and John Stockton as a role player with the Utah Jazz.
Donyell Lamar Marshall signed as a free agent with the Chicago Bulls on August 16, 2002.
Donyell Lamar Marshall played with Jalen Rose, Kendall Gill, Jay Williams, Eddy Curry, and Tyson Chandler during his time with the Chicago Bulls.
Donyell Lamar Marshall was traded from the Chicago Bulls to the Toronto Raptors along with Jalen Rose and Lonny Baxter on December 1, 2003.
Donyell Lamar Marshall tied Kobe Bryant's NBA record for three-point field goals made in one game by making 12 of 19 attempts against the Philadelphia 76ers on March 13, 2005.
Donyell Lamar Marshall was traded from the Toronto Raptors to the Cleveland Cavaliers along with Jalen Rose and Lonny Baxter on December 1, 2003.
Donyell Lamar Marshall helped the Cleveland Cavaliers to a victory over the New Jersey Nets in Game 6 of the Eastern Conference semifinals by making six three-pointers in May 2007.

Donyell Lamar Marshall made six three-pointers during the Cleveland Cavaliers' victory over the New Jersey Nets in Game 6 of the Eastern Conference semifinals, which propelled the Cavaliers to the NBA Eastern Conference finals against the Detroit Pistons and eventually the NBA finals against the San Antonio Spurs.
Donyell Lamar Marshall was traded from the Cleveland Cavaliers to the Seattle SuperSonics on February 21, 2008, in an 11-player deal involving three organizations.
The Seattle SuperSonics moved to Oklahoma City after Donyell Lamar Marshall's trade.
Donyell Lamar Marshall was waived by the Oklahoma City Thunder before the start of the new season following his trade from the Seattle SuperSonics.
Donyell Lamar Marshall agreed to terms with the Philadelphia 76ers on a one-year contract on September 1, 2008.
Donyell Lamar Marshall's goal for playing for the Philadelphia 76ers was to retire in his hometown.
Donyell Lamar Marshall played just 25 games for the Philadelphia 76ers and provided veteran leadership and three-point shooting.

Donyell Lamar Marshall played a key role in Philadelphia's game 1 victory over the Orlando Magic in the first round of the playoffs, scoring 11 points and making a three-pointer to tie the game in the final minute.
Donyell Lamar Marshall joined Comcast SportsNet as a post-game live analyst for the 76ers after retiring from the NBA on October 26, 2009.
Donyell Lamar Marshall left broadcasting on July 1, 2010, to become an assistant men's basketball coach of the George Washington Colonials under Karl Hobbs.
Donyell Lamar Marshall was announced as an assistant coach of the D-League's Maine Red Claws on November 3, 2011.
Donyell Lamar Marshall became an assistant coach of the Rider University men's basketball team in September 2013.
Donyell Lamar Marshall was largely responsible for the effective play of senior transfer center Matt Lopez and a second place regular season finish in the MAAC in 2014–15.
Donyell Lamar Marshall had a head coaching record at Central Connecticut State from April 6, 2016, to November 7, 2021.
Donyell Lamar Marshall won his first game as head coach of Central Connecticut on November 11, 2016, against Hartford with a score of 75-60.
Donyell Lamar Marshall and Central Connecticut mutually agreed to part ways after the 2021 season, ending his time at the school after five seasons.
Donyell Lamar Marshall became an assistant coach for the Greensboro Swarm of the NBA G League on October 24, 2021.
Lenny Moore is Donyell Marshall's great uncle and a Hall of Fame American football player.

Until November 7, 2016, Donyell Lamar Marshall held and shared the NBA record (with Kobe Bryant and Stephen Curry) for most three-point field goals made in a game after making 12 three-point field goals out of 19 attempts against the Philadelphia 76ers on March 13, 2005.
